    - id: MEMORY-BESTPRACTICE-001
      category: BESTPRACTICE
      scope: Global
      text: >-
        # Best practices: engineering rules for every agent on both lab machines


        One rule set, consolidated on 2026-11-06 at the operator's request from eight earlier Global memories of the two lab stores (listed under "Sources"). The operator's words are quoted under "Sources" at the end. It applies to all agents on both lab machines, LAB-OMARCHY and PAYTON-LEGION2, and across workspaces.


        ## 1. Code documentation: every code change


        1.1. Every code change carries proper XML documentation that describes the affected code.


        1.2. That documentation includes a dated change log entry listing the associated canonical requirement ids and descriptive acceptance-criterion ids, plus what changed and why.


        1.3. Maintain purpose, behavior, parameters, returns and exceptions, as applicable.


        1.4. Preserve earlier change log entries.


        1.5. Verify every id against the canonical workspace records. Do not invent traceability or imply acceptance.


        1.6. Where XML documentation is unsupported, use the language's native documentation comments with equivalent dated requirement, acceptance-criterion and change fields.


        1.7. This is source documentation, not a request for per-PR release notes or an unrelated retrospective sweep.


        1.8. Workspace guidance and examples: AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/code-documentation-traceability.mdc.


        ## 2. Test runs: targeted after an edit, full gate set once at phase exit


        2.1. After an edit, a BDPv4 mock gate or binding runs only the changed test classes, through the Nuke target TestGroups (TR-MCP-NUKE-020), never raw dotnet test.


        2.2. The command: ./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups "<test project>:<Class>[,<Class>...]" ["<project>:<Class>..." ...] --test-run-id <run id>


        2.3. TestGroups writes one TRX per project under TestResults/<run id>/groups/<project>/<project>.trx.


        2.4. It selects the named classes whatever their category, but excludes cases tagged for the other platform (Platform!=Windows on Linux, Platform!=Linux on Windows).


        2.5. It fails on an unknown project, a group that selects no case, a named class that ran no case, or any failed or skipped case.


        2.6. The full gate set (Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, Build.Tests and ValidateTraceability, on both hosts) runs once, at the final head, to validate phase exit before hostile validation.


        2.7. If a gate then fails: fix it, test the fix through TestGroups, and run the full gate set once more at the new head.


        2.8. In McpServer, TestGroups is on branch fix/unit-suite-green-20261019 (PR 87) until that pull request merges into develop.


        ## 3. Windows paths


        3.1. Use forward slashes in Windows paths (for example F:/GitHub/vice-sharp and C:/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe), including paths handed to MSYS2 tools such as gcc, and in scripts, configs and generated build or link arguments.


        ## 4. Unit tests and integration tests


        4.1. Unit tests and integration tests live in separate projects and are correctly tagged.


        4.2. Unit tests exercise code in isolation, using controlled mocks or fakes as needed.


        4.3. Any test that depends on the environment is an integration test, and is never classified or run as a unit test.


        4.4. Apply this distinction to test-project ownership, category tags, Nuke groups and gates, and reported test evidence, across workspaces.


        4.5. Preserve BDPv4's green, discriminating mock gates before production changes.


        ## 5. Emulators


        5.1. When the work that needs an emulator is complete, shut the emulator down to a known state and freeze it.


        5.2. Restore it from that frozen state only when active work needs it.


        5.3. Never leave an emulator running idle and consuming resources after its work is complete.


        ## 6. Git worktrees


        6.1. Create git worktrees inside the owning repository's workspace directory, never as sibling directories beside it. Example: TruckMate worktrees belong under F:/GitHub/TruckMate/.worktrees/<name>. This applies to every repository.


        ## 7. NuGet warnings


        7.1. NuGet warnings may never be ignored.


        7.2. Do not suppress NU1902, NU1903 or any other NuGet warning, downgrade an enforced warning gate, disable NuGet audit, or use a local or bootstrap exception to bypass them.


        7.3. Repair the dependency issue within the authorized scope, or report the exact affected dependency and the scope decision it needs.


        7.4. The operator explicitly rejected a local-only advisory warning override for the pinned FeatureFlags tool bootstrap.


        ## 8. Mistakes and accountability


        8.1. Acknowledge your mistakes, state the rule you broke, and account for the wasted usage and time.


        8.2. State the specific action and its consequence.


        8.3. Give measured usage and elapsed time when available, and keep measured facts apart from estimates and unavailable figures.


        ## Sources


        - Rule 1: operator instruction of 2026-11-02, as recorded in the LAB-OMARCHY store's MEMORY-FACT-008 version 1.

        - Rule 2: MEMORY-PROCESS-012 version 2 (set up 2026-11-02 for all agents on both lab machines; version 2 added TR-MCP-NUKE-020 AC-4 and AC-5). Operator, 2026-10-27T21:46 local, verbatim: "Stop running full test suites after one edit.  Test what you changed and save full suite execution for validatin that its time to exit the phase and run HV." Operator, 2026-11-02, verbatim: "Use dedicated targets or an integration target that accepts an array of tests groups to run."

        - Rule 3: MEMORY-PROCEDURE-005 version 1. Operator (Payton), 2026-10-20 08:19, verbatim: "The lab rules are to use foreward slashes on Windows."

        - Rule 4: operator directive of 2026-11-05, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-FACT-008 version 1.

        - Rule 5: operator global directive of 2026-11-05, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-FACT-009 version 1.

        - Rule 6: operator directive of 2026-11-01, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-PREFERENCE-008 version 1.

        - Rule 7: operator directive of 2026-11-03, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-PROCESS-013 version 1.

        - Rule 8: operator global rule of 2026-11-05, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-PROCESS-014 version 1.

        - The consolidation: operator, 2026-11-06, verbatim, replying to each of rules 1 to 3 in the LAB-OMARCHY memory list: "Add to a consolidated best practices global memory."; and to each of rules 4 to 8 in the PAYTON-LEGION2 memory list: "Add to the combined best practices."

        ## 9. Scope control and verification rigor


        9.1. Scope creep means adding requirements or product behavior the operator did not request or approve.


        9.2. Thoroughness is not scope creep. Within approved requirements, make tests, negative controls, validation, evidence, metadata, documentation, and review artifacts thorough, thoughtful, precise, accurate, internally consistent, and clean in both function and form.


        9.3. Add or strengthen verification when it materially proves the approved behavior or exposes defects in an in-scope project artifact. Do not turn testing rigor into an unapproved product requirement.


        9.4. Do not use scope control as an excuse to leave a known defect in an in-scope project artifact. Repair the defect or present the specific requirement decision the operator owns.


        ## Source


        - Operator guidance of 2026-11-07: "There is a difference between scope creep and being thorough, precise and accurate. I do not want scope creep, which is where you add requirements I didn't ask for. I do want thorough and thoughtful testing." The operator directed that this be cleaned up as general guidance and added to the best-practices Global memory on both lab stores.

    - id: MEMORY-HV-001
      category: HV
      scope: Global
      text: >-
        # HV rules: hostile-validation rules for every agent and every HV round


        One rule set, merged on 2026-11-06 from MEMORY-PROCESS-010 (version 2) and MEMORY-PROCESS-013 (version 1), reformatted and refined at the operator's request. The operator's words are quoted under "Sources" at the end. "Task" means one task of the plan under review (in McpServer, one implementation task of the plan's TODO). "Change under review" means the commits or edits the HV round reviews. A requirement is "in flux" when a change under review adds, changes or implements it.


        ## 1. Verdicts and scores


        1.1. Every HV round returns an overall verdict, AGREE or DISAGREE, with an accuracy score and a completeness score. The overall verdict is AGREE only when both scores are 98 or more.


        1.2. Every HV round also returns a verdict for each task it adjudicates (rule 3.2): AGREE or DISAGREE, with that task's own accuracy and completeness scores. A task's AGREE needs both of its scores at 98 or more.


        1.3. The per-task verdicts are the operator's own gates. They are not extra approval gates added by an agent.


        ## 2. Marking tasks completed, and regressions


        2.1. A task that clears its own HV AGREE is marked completed in the plan and in its TODO, through the agent's plugin. The completion cites that round's request JSONL, its response JSONL and the session-log turn that holds the verdict.


        2.2. A task without its own AGREE stays open, whatever the overall verdict.


        2.3. A completed task is not adjudicated again as an incomplete task. It is checked only for regression, when rule 3.3 selects it. A regression is any finding that would invalidate a completed task. A task with a regression is reopened, because no done state may stand while a failure is outstanding, and it stays open until a later round clears it again.


        2.4. Every regression is called out in the review summary, by task, with the finding and the requirement it touches.


        2.5. Per-task verdicts keep each round tied to the plan's tasks, which helps against scope creep.


        ## 3. Review scope: the requirements matrix


        3.1. The reviewer builds and keeps, and returns with its verdict, a matrix of: the requirements of each task, and the requirements of each change under review. The matrix shows which requirements are in flux and which tasks share them.


        3.2. An open task with at least one requirement in flux is adjudicated in full and gets its own verdict and scores (rule 1.2).


        3.3. A completed task that shares a requirement in flux gets regression attention only (rule 2.3). Its result is either "no regression" or a regression finding.


        3.4. A task with no requirement being adjudicated in this round is not reviewed, unless the operator requests a holistic review. This holds for open tasks as well as completed ones: an open task out of scope stays open for that round. For example, an HV midway through a plan, such as a phase gate, still sees requirements and tasks of other phases; they are out of scope for that review. The matrix still lists them, marked out of scope.


        ## 4. What every HV request contains


        4.1. Every task of the plan under review, each with a fixed number and its state (open or completed), and the changes under review.


        4.2. The requirement to return the matrix (rule 3.1), a verdict and both scores for each task adjudicated in full (rule 3.2), a regression result for each task selected for regression (rule 3.3), and the regressions called out in the summary (rule 2.4).


        4.3. Rule 6 (infrastructure failures), stated explicitly.


        4.4. Complete paired request and response JSONL, and the complete verdict artifacts, are kept for every round.


        ## 5. Interpreting findings


        5.1. Reason about the context and the underlying failure pattern of each finding. Do not merely patch the cited line or satisfy the reviewer's wording.


        5.2. Understand the affected user outcome and the claim the evidence is meant to support.


        5.3. Verify each finding against authoritative sources.


        5.4. Examine related instances and the end-to-end chain among requirements, design, implementation, tests, evidence, documentation, publication and actual deployment, as applicable.


        5.5. Check whether a proposed fix and its tests address the underlying class of failure without introducing new gaps.


        5.6. Keep observed facts apart from inference, unverified claims and unresolved decisions.


        5.7. Preserve full review receipts, and report every FAIL and every UNKNOWN.


        5.8. Apply the existing plan and review rules. Do not invent additional approval gates, and do not treat passing a replacement check as proof of the user outcome.


        ## 6. Infrastructure failures


        6.1. Infrastructure failures have no bearing on HV AGREE when sufficient review evidence is present. Judge the requested product, plan, requirements, code, tests and retained evidence on their merits.


        6.2. MCP availability, live memory-loading failures, triage submission, session-log persistence or readback, and other infrastructure failures must not by themselves force DISAGREE, lower a score or block acceptance when the needed evidence is otherwise available.


        6.3. Record infrastructure failures separately, as operational issues. Use the supported failsafe and retry persistence without delaying the substantive verdict.


        6.4. If a failure actually prevents access to evidence needed for a specific criterion, name that missing evidence and the affected criterion honestly. Never invent a PASS or an AGREE.


        6.5. Rule 6 supersedes older profile or template rules that made infrastructure persistence or live memory loading a prerequisite for HV AGREE.


        ## Sources


        - Rules 5.1 to 5.8: operator instruction of 2026-10-29, as recorded in MEMORY-PROCESS-010 version 1.

1	# PLAN-FRENEMY-002: Four-agent reasoning integration test
2	
3	Status: In progress. The operator approved implementation on 2026-11-07. Hostile review R12 returned DISAGREE at 95 accuracy and 94 completeness with 29 PASS, 5 FAIL, and 0 UNKNOWN. Task 1 had no regression; Task 3 cleared AGREE at 98/98; Tasks 2 and 4 remain open. All five R12 findings are remediated: the direct controls are present, the tested artifacts are committed at `86402e4e64e3d06183f16a3323401c014e99fc2f`, the append-only corrections are retained, and the authoritative TODO is current. The next reviewer packet supplies the post-documentation final-head deterministic TRX. Completion requires the independent overall and in-scope task AGREE at 98/98 or higher with no unresolved applicable FAIL or UNKNOWN.
4	
5	## Outcome
6	
7	Add one opt-in integration test for the current Frenemy server. Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, and Cline CLI will each answer the same five acceptance-criteria questions at medium effort. Each answer will be scored by the other three agents. A run passes only when every peer score is at least 50 and all required evidence is archived for human review.
8	
9	Requirement records:
10	
11	- `FR-FRENEMY-117`: Four-agent reasoning integration review.
12	- `TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121`: Four-agent reasoning integration harness.
13	- `TEST-FRENEMY-117`: Validate four-agent reasoning and peer review.
14	- Mapping: `FR-FRENEMY-117` to `TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121` and `TEST-FRENEMY-117`.
15	
16	## Scope boundary
17	
18	In scope:
19	
20	- A JavaScript test harness and JavaScript assertions.
21	- Independent scripted fakes and negative controls before the live harness.
22	- Nuke and PowerShell orchestration needed to select the test, retain TRX, and create the archive.
23	- The existing caller-side `codex exec` path.
24	- The current Frenemy `ask_claude`, `ask_grok`, and `ask_cline` read-only tools.
25	- Directly related test documentation and validation receipts.
26	
27	Out of scope:
28	
29	- New Frenemy tools, services, APIs, job systems, schedulers, or persistence.
30	- Changes to relay product behavior, write-mode behavior, permissions, authentication, installers, agent plugins, or workstation configuration.
31	- C# product code or C# tests. `build/Build.cs` remains Nuke orchestration only.
32	- Collecting internal hidden reasoning or external CLI internals that the current Frenemy boundary does not expose.
33	- Redacting the orchestration conversation or agent answers. Credentials and environment dumps are never collected in the first place.
34	
35	## Source-pinned baseline
36	
37	- `README.md` describes the asymmetric four-agent design: Claude calls Codex through `codex exec`; Codex reaches Claude, Grok, and Cline through Frenemy.
38	- `CLAUDE-codex-section.md` defines the existing caller-side Codex path.
39	- `ask-claude-mcp.mjs` exposes the six existing read/write tools. The new test uses only `ask_claude`, `ask_grok`, and `ask_cline`.
40	- `ask-claude-mcp.mjs` already accepts `effort` for Claude, Grok, and Cline and maps it to each native interface.
41	- `build/Build.cs` and `build/Invoke-RelayTests.ps1` are the existing Nuke and PowerShell test orchestration seams.
42	- The local `codex exec --help` receipt confirms read-only execution, JSONL output, absolute working-directory selection, and config overrides. Codex medium effort will use `-c model_reasoning_effort=medium`.
43	
44	## Canonical questions
45	
46	The exact texts and rubrics are acceptance criteria `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-Q01` through `Q05`. The test will load one version-controlled fixture containing those exact values. It will not generate, paraphrase, replace, or select questions dynamically.
47	
48	1. Math: independent component failures across five days. Canonical result: `1 - 0.98^5 = 0.0960792032`, approximately 9.61 percent.
49	2. Physics: a 2.0 kg block drops 5.0 m and crosses 10.0 m at kinetic-friction coefficient 0.20. Canonical result: 58.8 J final kinetic energy and approximately 7.67 m/s.
50	3. History: explain the Provisional Government's loss of authority from February through October 1917 by weighing and connecting at least three rubric factors.
51	4. Chemistry: acetic-acid/acetate buffer after 0.050 mol HCl. Canonical result: 0.050 mol acetate, 0.250 mol acid, pH approximately 4.06.
52	5. Economics: linear demand and supply with a 10 dollar seller tax. Canonical results: no-tax `P=20, Q=80`; tax `Pb=26, Ps=16, Q=68`; burdens 6 and 4 dollars; revenue 680 dollars; deadweight loss 60 dollars.
53	
54	The MCP requirement record is the authoritative wording. The repository fixture will be checked byte-for-byte against a version-controlled projection of those criteria during implementation.
55	
56	## Locked orchestration protocol
57	
58	The participant IDs are `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, and `cline`.
59	
60	For each question, in order:
61	
62	1. Start four answer sessions concurrently, one per participant. The prompt includes the exact question and rubric identifier, requests a concise answer with supporting reasoning, forbids workspace inspection because the question is self-contained, and explicitly sets medium effort.
63	2. Wait for all four answers. Any launch failure, timeout, tool error, empty answer, or wrong question identity fails the run. No automatic retry or substitute agent is allowed.
64	3. Start four review sessions concurrently, one per participant. Each reviewer receives the exact rubric and the other three answers, never its own answer, and returns three judgments.
65	4. Validate each judgment as strict JSON with `questionId`, `subjectAgent`, `reviewerAgent`, integer `accuracy` from 0 through 100, `rationale`, and `rubricFindings`.
66	5. Require all 12 judgments for that question to be distinct and valid before advancing to the next question.
67	
68	This produces 40 individual sessions: 20 answer sessions and 20 bundled peer-review sessions. It produces 20 answers and 60 peer judgments. A run passes only if every one of the 60 peer judgments is at least 50. The arithmetic mean is reported for human convenience but is not the gate.
69	
70	Medium-effort bindings:
71	
72	- Claude: `ask_claude` with `effort: "medium"`.
73	- Codex: `codex exec --sandbox read-only --json -c model_reasoning_effort=medium` with the prompt on standard input.
74	- Grok: `ask_grok` with `effort: "medium"`.
75	- Cline: `ask_cline` with `provider: "openai-codex"`, `model: "gpt-5.6-luna"`, and `effort: "medium"`, preserving the operator's existing Cline test configuration.
76	
77	Claude, Grok, and Cline run through a fresh Frenemy stdio relay process for each individual session. Each transcript therefore contains the complete boundary-visible initialization, tool request, tool response, relay standard error, exit state, selected effort, and timestamps for that session. Codex transcripts retain its complete JSONL event stream and final response. The test does not claim access to hidden reasoning or target-internal events that the current relay does not expose.
78	
79	## Artifact contract
80	
81	The run root is `TestResults/<run-id>/four-agent-reasoning/`. The final archive is `TestResults/<run-id>/four-agent-reasoning-review.zip`.
82	
83	Required contents:
84	
85	- `manifest.json`: run ID, git head, host, run status, participant targets, requested provider/model/effort, timestamps, tested-source hashes, and relative paths, sizes, and SHA-256 for every retained file. Individual exit states remain in the session transcripts.
86	- `questions.json`: exact five questions and canonical rubrics.
87	- `orchestration.jsonl`: every orchestration event in order, including complete prompts, answers, peer-review prompts, peer-review results, failures, and state transitions.
88	- `sessions/<agent>/<questionId>/answer.jsonl` for all 20 answer sessions.
89	- `sessions/<agent>/<questionId>/review.jsonl` for all 20 peer-review sessions.
90	- `answers.json`, `peer-judgments.json`, and `summary.json`.
91	- The JUnit source report, converted TRX, standard-error logs, and archive-validation receipt.
92	
93	Each JSONL entry carries `runId`, `questionId`, `phase`, `agent`, `sessionId`, sortable local timestamp, direction, event type, and payload. JSON and JSONL are generated from objects, never handwritten strings.
94	
95	The archive is finalized in a `finally` path. A failed or interrupted run retains every artifact obtained before failure and an explicit terminal failure record. Missing files, duplicate participant/question/role identities, mismatched hashes, absent medium-effort evidence, or an unreadable ZIP fail the test.
96	
97	## Implementation phases
98	
99	### Phase 1: Requirement baseline and exact fixture
100	
101	1. Re-read `FR-FRENEMY-117`, `TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121`, `TEST-FRENEMY-117`, and their mapping at implementation start.
102	2. Verify all five exact question criteria and every operational criterion remain present with `isSatisfied: false`.
103	3. Add a version-controlled question fixture projected from `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-Q01` through `Q05` and a mechanical drift check.
104	
105	Gate: requirement and mapping readback succeeds, question text and rubric hashes match the fixture, and no product code has changed.
106	
107	### Phase 2: BDPv4 mock-green gate
108	
109	Add first:
110	
111	- `tests/fixtures/four-agent-reasoning-questions.json`.
112	- `tests/unit/four-agent-reasoning.contract.test.mjs` with class identity `FourAgentReasoningMockTests`.
113	- Independent scripted answer and review providers that do not call the relay or real CLIs.
114	
115	The correct fixture must prove 4 participants, 5 questions, 20 answers, 40 sessions, 60 judgments, all medium effort, all peer scores at least 50, and a complete archive manifest.
116	
117	Negative controls must independently reject:
118	
119	- missing participant, answer, session, or judgment;
120	- wrong or duplicated question identity;
121	- non-medium effort;
122	- self-review;
123	- duplicate subject/reviewer pair;
124	- malformed, non-integer, or out-of-range score;
125	- a score of 49;
126	- agent failure, timeout, or empty answer;
127	- incomplete orchestration JSONL, missing session transcript, manifest mismatch, hash mismatch, or unreadable archive.
128	
129	Run only the changed mock class through Nuke:
130	
131	```powershell
132	.\build.ps1 TestGroups --groups "Frenemy.Relay.UnitTests:FourAgentReasoningMockTests" --test-run-id <yyyyMMddTHHmmss>-four-agent-mock
133	```
134	
135	Gate: correct scripted data passes, every deliberate mutation reaches and is rejected by its intended assertion inside a passing suite, and TRX reports 0 failed and 0 skipped. The unit contract uses only deterministic version-controlled fixtures and independent scripted fakes, does not read harvested live data or integration artifacts, and produces the same result whether or not live data exists.
136	
137	### Phase 3: Live integration binding
138	
139	Add:
140	
141	- `tests/integration/four-agent-reasoning.integration.test.mjs` with class identity `FourAgentReasoningIntegrationTests`.
142	- `tests/integration/four-agent-reasoning.archive.test.mjs` with class identity `FourAgentReasoningArchiveIntegrationTests`.
143	- Test-side helpers under `tests/contracts/` for the shared fixture, strict peer-judgment validation, archive validation, and process-boundary transcript writing.

145	- Nuke parameters for absolute Claude, Codex, Grok, and Cline executables.
146	- `Invoke-RelayTests.ps1` routing for the new unit and integration class names, environment, TRX conversion, and always-run archive finalization.
147	- A narrow prompt correction in `tests/native/production-native-qualification.test.mjs`, mapped to `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-115-04`, that asks Cline to preserve the qualification fixture's required LF byte. The exact byte assertion is unchanged, and this is test qualification only, not product behavior.
148	
149	The live test reuses the same fixture, counts, identities, schema checks, score gate, and archive assertions from Phase 2. It does not weaken an assertion or replace an expected value with live output.
150	
151	Test inventory and requirement mapping:
152	
153	- `FourAgentReasoningMockTests` proves the common contract for `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-Q01` through `Q05` and `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-06` through `08`, including independent negative controls.
154	- `FourAgentReasoningIntegrationTests` binds the same questions, rubrics, medium-effort configuration, counts, score gate, session evidence, and failure behavior to the current Frenemy and Codex process boundaries.
155	- `FourAgentReasoningArchiveIntegrationTests` opens and validates the live ZIP bytes, then invokes `assertFourAgentArchiveEvidence` against the independently derived member set, contents, archive hash, external validation receipt, manifest, and current tested-source bytes. It covers `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-08`, `AC-FRENEMY-117-04`, and `AC-TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121-05`.
156	
157	Before executing modified PowerShell, run the PowerShell parser and PSScriptAnalyzer at Warning and Error severity and fix every finding.
158

161	```powershell

163	```
164	
165	Gate: the live run returns 20 answers, 60 distinct peer judgments at 50 or higher, 0 failed and 0 skipped tests, 40 complete session transcripts, a valid TRX, and a mechanically validated ZIP with SHA-256.

167	### Phase 4: Regression, documentation, and hostile review
168	
169	1. Run the focused unit and integration classes through Nuke after each related edit.

# PLAN-FRENEMY-002: Four-agent reasoning integration test

Status: In progress. The operator approved implementation on 2026-11-07. Hostile review R12 returned DISAGREE at 95 accuracy and 94 completeness with 29 PASS, 5 FAIL, and 0 UNKNOWN. Task 1 had no regression; Task 3 cleared AGREE at 98/98; Tasks 2 and 4 remain open. All five R12 findings are remediated: the direct controls are present, the tested artifacts are committed at `86402e4e64e3d06183f16a3323401c014e99fc2f`, the append-only corrections are retained, and the authoritative TODO is current. The next reviewer packet supplies the post-documentation final-head deterministic TRX. Completion requires the independent overall and in-scope task AGREE at 98/98 or higher with no unresolved applicable FAIL or UNKNOWN.

## Outcome

Add one opt-in integration test for the current Frenemy server. Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, and Cline CLI will each answer the same five acceptance-criteria questions at medium effort. Each answer will be scored by the other three agents. A run passes only when every peer score is at least 50 and all required evidence is archived for human review.

Requirement records:

- `FR-FRENEMY-117`: Four-agent reasoning integration review.
- `TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121`: Four-agent reasoning integration harness.
- `TEST-FRENEMY-117`: Validate four-agent reasoning and peer review.
- Mapping: `FR-FRENEMY-117` to `TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121` and `TEST-FRENEMY-117`.

## Scope boundary

In scope:

- A JavaScript test harness and JavaScript assertions.
- Independent scripted fakes and negative controls before the live harness.
- Nuke and PowerShell orchestration needed to select the test, retain TRX, and create the archive.
- The existing caller-side `codex exec` path.
- The current Frenemy `ask_claude`, `ask_grok`, and `ask_cline` read-only tools.
- Directly related test documentation and validation receipts.

Out of scope:

- New Frenemy tools, services, APIs, job systems, schedulers, or persistence.
- Changes to relay product behavior, write-mode behavior, permissions, authentication, installers, agent plugins, or workstation configuration.
- C# product code or C# tests. `build/Build.cs` remains Nuke orchestration only.
- Collecting internal hidden reasoning or external CLI internals that the current Frenemy boundary does not expose.
- Redacting the orchestration conversation or agent answers. Credentials and environment dumps are never collected in the first place.

## Source-pinned baseline

- `README.md` describes the asymmetric four-agent design: Claude calls Codex through `codex exec`; Codex reaches Claude, Grok, and Cline through Frenemy.
- `CLAUDE-codex-section.md` defines the existing caller-side Codex path.
- `ask-claude-mcp.mjs` exposes the six existing read/write tools. The new test uses only `ask_claude`, `ask_grok`, and `ask_cline`.
- `ask-claude-mcp.mjs` already accepts `effort` for Claude, Grok, and Cline and maps it to each native interface.
- `build/Build.cs` and `build/Invoke-RelayTests.ps1` are the existing Nuke and PowerShell test orchestration seams.
- The local `codex exec --help` receipt confirms read-only execution, JSONL output, absolute working-directory selection, and config overrides. Codex medium effort will use `-c model_reasoning_effort=medium`.

## Canonical questions

The exact texts and rubrics are acceptance criteria `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-Q01` through `Q05`. The test will load one version-controlled fixture containing those exact values. It will not generate, paraphrase, replace, or select questions dynamically.

1. Math: independent component failures across five days. Canonical result: `1 - 0.98^5 = 0.0960792032`, approximately 9.61 percent.
2. Physics: a 2.0 kg block drops 5.0 m and crosses 10.0 m at kinetic-friction coefficient 0.20. Canonical result: 58.8 J final kinetic energy and approximately 7.67 m/s.
3. History: explain the Provisional Government's loss of authority from February through October 1917 by weighing and connecting at least three rubric factors.
4. Chemistry: acetic-acid/acetate buffer after 0.050 mol HCl. Canonical result: 0.050 mol acetate, 0.250 mol acid, pH approximately 4.06.
5. Economics: linear demand and supply with a 10 dollar seller tax. Canonical results: no-tax `P=20, Q=80`; tax `Pb=26, Ps=16, Q=68`; burdens 6 and 4 dollars; revenue 680 dollars; deadweight loss 60 dollars.

The MCP requirement record is the authoritative wording. The repository fixture will be checked byte-for-byte against a version-controlled projection of those criteria during implementation.

## Locked orchestration protocol

The participant IDs are `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, and `cline`.

For each question, in order:

1. Start four answer sessions concurrently, one per participant. The prompt includes the exact question and rubric identifier, requests a concise answer with supporting reasoning, forbids workspace inspection because the question is self-contained, and explicitly sets medium effort.
2. Wait for all four answers. Any launch failure, timeout, tool error, empty answer, or wrong question identity fails the run. No automatic retry or substitute agent is allowed.
3. Start four review sessions concurrently, one per participant. Each reviewer receives the exact rubric and the other three answers, never its own answer, and returns three judgments.
4. Validate each judgment as strict JSON with `questionId`, `subjectAgent`, `reviewerAgent`, integer `accuracy` from 0 through 100, `rationale`, and `rubricFindings`.
5. Require all 12 judgments for that question to be distinct and valid before advancing to the next question.

This produces 40 individual sessions: 20 answer sessions and 20 bundled peer-review sessions. It produces 20 answers and 60 peer judgments. A run passes only if every one of the 60 peer judgments is at least 50. The arithmetic mean is reported for human convenience but is not the gate.

Medium-effort bindings:

- Claude: `ask_claude` with `effort: "medium"`.
- Codex: `codex exec --sandbox read-only --json -c model_reasoning_effort=medium` with the prompt on standard input.
- Grok: `ask_grok` with `effort: "medium"`.
- Cline: `ask_cline` with `provider: "openai-codex"`, `model: "gpt-5.6-luna"`, and `effort: "medium"`, preserving the operator's existing Cline test configuration.

Claude, Grok, and Cline run through a fresh Frenemy stdio relay process for each individual session. Each transcript therefore contains the complete boundary-visible initialization, tool request, tool response, relay standard error, exit state, selected effort, and timestamps for that session. Codex transcripts retain its complete JSONL event stream and final response. The test does not claim access to hidden reasoning or target-internal events that the current relay does not expose.

## Artifact contract

The run root is `TestResults/<run-id>/four-agent-reasoning/`. The final archive is `TestResults/<run-id>/four-agent-reasoning-review.zip`.

Required contents:

- `manifest.json`: run ID, git head, host, run status, participant targets, requested provider/model/effort, timestamps, tested-source hashes, and relative paths, sizes, and SHA-256 for every retained file. Individual exit states remain in the session transcripts.
- `questions.json`: exact five questions and canonical rubrics.
- `orchestration.jsonl`: every orchestration event in order, including complete prompts, answers, peer-review prompts, peer-review results, failures, and state transitions.
- `sessions/<agent>/<questionId>/answer.jsonl` for all 20 answer sessions.
- `sessions/<agent>/<questionId>/review.jsonl` for all 20 peer-review sessions.
- `answers.json`, `peer-judgments.json`, and `summary.json`.
- The JUnit source report, converted TRX, standard-error logs, and archive-validation receipt.

Each JSONL entry carries `runId`, `questionId`, `phase`, `agent`, `sessionId`, sortable local timestamp, direction, event type, and payload. JSON and JSONL are generated from objects, never handwritten strings.

The archive is finalized in a `finally` path. A failed or interrupted run retains every artifact obtained before failure and an explicit terminal failure record. Missing files, duplicate participant/question/role identities, mismatched hashes, absent medium-effort evidence, or an unreadable ZIP fail the test.

## Implementation phases

### Phase 1: Requirement baseline and exact fixture

1. Re-read `FR-FRENEMY-117`, `TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121`, `TEST-FRENEMY-117`, and their mapping at implementation start.
2. Verify all five exact question criteria and every operational criterion remain present with `isSatisfied: false`.
3. Add a version-controlled question fixture projected from `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-Q01` through `Q05` and a mechanical drift check.

Gate: requirement and mapping readback succeeds, question text and rubric hashes match the fixture, and no product code has changed.

### Phase 2: BDPv4 mock-green gate

Add first:

- `tests/fixtures/four-agent-reasoning-questions.json`.
- `tests/unit/four-agent-reasoning.contract.test.mjs` with class identity `FourAgentReasoningMockTests`.
- Independent scripted answer and review providers that do not call the relay or real CLIs.

The correct fixture must prove 4 participants, 5 questions, 20 answers, 40 sessions, 60 judgments, all medium effort, all peer scores at least 50, and a complete archive manifest.

Negative controls must independently reject:

- missing participant, answer, session, or judgment;
- wrong or duplicated question identity;
- non-medium effort;
- self-review;
- duplicate subject/reviewer pair;
- malformed, non-integer, or out-of-range score;
- a score of 49;
- agent failure, timeout, or empty answer;
- incomplete orchestration JSONL, missing session transcript, manifest mismatch, hash mismatch, or unreadable archive.

Run only the changed mock class through Nuke:

```powershell
.\build.ps1 TestGroups --groups "Frenemy.Relay.UnitTests:FourAgentReasoningMockTests" --test-run-id <yyyyMMddTHHmmss>-four-agent-mock
```

Gate: correct scripted data passes, every deliberate mutation reaches and is rejected by its intended assertion inside a passing suite, and TRX reports 0 failed and 0 skipped. The unit contract uses only deterministic version-controlled fixtures and independent scripted fakes, does not read harvested live data or integration artifacts, and produces the same result whether or not live data exists.

### Phase 3: Live integration binding

Add:

- `tests/integration/four-agent-reasoning.integration.test.mjs` with class identity `FourAgentReasoningIntegrationTests`.
- `tests/integration/four-agent-reasoning.archive.test.mjs` with class identity `FourAgentReasoningArchiveIntegrationTests`.
- Test-side helpers under `tests/contracts/` for the shared fixture, strict peer-judgment validation, archive validation, and process-boundary transcript writing.
- `FourAgentReasoningIntegration` and `VerifyFourAgentReasoningMocks` Nuke targets.
- Nuke parameters for absolute Claude, Codex, Grok, and Cline executables.
- `Invoke-RelayTests.ps1` routing for the new unit and integration class names, environment, TRX conversion, and always-run archive finalization.
- A narrow prompt correction in `tests/native/production-native-qualification.test.mjs`, mapped to `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-115-04`, that asks Cline to preserve the qualification fixture's required LF byte. The exact byte assertion is unchanged, and this is test qualification only, not product behavior.

The live test reuses the same fixture, counts, identities, schema checks, score gate, and archive assertions from Phase 2. It does not weaken an assertion or replace an expected value with live output.

Test inventory and requirement mapping:

- `FourAgentReasoningMockTests` proves the common contract for `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-Q01` through `Q05` and `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-06` through `08`, including independent negative controls.
- `FourAgentReasoningIntegrationTests` binds the same questions, rubrics, medium-effort configuration, counts, score gate, session evidence, and failure behavior to the current Frenemy and Codex process boundaries.
- `FourAgentReasoningArchiveIntegrationTests` opens and validates the live ZIP bytes, then invokes `assertFourAgentArchiveEvidence` against the independently derived member set, contents, archive hash, external validation receipt, manifest, and current tested-source bytes. It covers `AC-TEST-FRENEMY-117-08`, `AC-FRENEMY-117-04`, and `AC-TR-FRENEMY-ORCH-121-05`.

Before executing modified PowerShell, run the PowerShell parser and PSScriptAnalyzer at Warning and Error severity and fix every finding.

Focused live command:

```powershell
.\build.ps1 FourAgentReasoningIntegration --claude-executable <absolute-path> --codex-executable <absolute-path> --grok-executable <absolute-path> --cline-executable <absolute-path> --test-run-id <yyyyMMddTHHmmss>-four-agent-live
```

Gate: the live run returns 20 answers, 60 distinct peer judgments at 50 or higher, 0 failed and 0 skipped tests, 40 complete session transcripts, a valid TRX, and a mechanically validated ZIP with SHA-256.

### Phase 4: Regression, documentation, and hostile review

1. Run the focused unit and integration classes through Nuke after each related edit.
2. At the final head, run the repository's full applicable Nuke `Validate` target once on the current host, followed by the opt-in live target once at that same head.
3. Update only the directly related test design, validation status, and documentation navigation.
4. Retain commands, executable versions, git head, TRX files, archive path/hash, assertion counts, and all failure output.
5. Send Claude Opus 5.5 high the complete in-scope chat log, plan, requirement readbacks, source, tests, TRX, archive manifest, and validation receipts exactly as produced. Do not redact mistakes or failures. Credentials are excluded by not collecting them.
6. The reviewer reads the supplied evidence and does not build or run tests. Persist the full request/response JSONL and full verdict in the MCP session log.

Gate: overall and task verdicts are AGREE with accuracy at least 98, completeness at least 98, 0 unresolved applicable FAIL, and 0 unresolved applicable UNKNOWN. Only then may the TODO or requirements be marked complete.

Task completion records:

- Task 1 completed at hostile review R3 with AGREE at 99 accuracy and 99 completeness, 7 PASS, 0 FAIL, and 0 UNKNOWN. Receipts: `docs/receipts/hv/20261107T124610-four-agent-reasoning-r3/request.jsonl`, `docs/receipts/hv/20261107T124610-four-agent-reasoning-r3/response.jsonl`, reviewer session-log turn `119971`.
- Task 3 completed at hostile review R5 with AGREE at 98 accuracy and 98 completeness. Receipts: `docs/receipts/hv/20261107T142337-four-agent-reasoning-r5/request.jsonl`, `docs/receipts/hv/20261107T142337-four-agent-reasoning-r5/response.jsonl`, reviewer session-log turn `120007`.
- R8 reopened Task 3 because a failed parallel answer batch retained four transcripts but recorded only the first completed answer and failed session. Task 3 remained open until the repaired harness proved every settled session and orchestration outcome was retained before the batch failure was raised.

Receipts: `docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/request.jsonl`, `docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/response.jsonl`, and `docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/verdict.md`.

## Failure and rollback behavior

- A live failure never triggers product changes, authentication changes, retries, provider/model substitution, or host/plugin repair.

- Rollback removes only the newly added four-agent test files and the exact Nuke/PowerShell routing additions, and restores only the prior Cline qualification prompt in `tests/native/production-native-qualification.test.mjs`. Use suitable test hosts with the native CLIs available. Record which CLI versions were exercised. The operator's workstation and plugins are outside the test denominator.

function firstAssertionLine(error) {
  return error.message.split("\n", 1)[0];
}

const reachedDirectControlMessages = [];

function assertReachedControl(action, expectedMessage) {
  let observedError;
  try {
    action();
  }
  catch (error) {
    observedError = error;
  }
  assert.ok(observedError, "direct negative control unexpectedly passed");
  const observedMessage = firstAssertionLine(observedError);
  assert.match(observedMessage, expectedMessage);
  reachedDirectControlMessages.push(observedMessage);
}

function reachedMessageMatchesLiteral(reachedMessage, literalMessage) {
  const escapedParts = literalMessage.split("*").map((part) => part.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/gu, "\\$&"));
  return new RegExp(`^${escapedParts.join(".+")}$`, "u").test(reachedMessage);
}

$hits = @(git grep -l -F -e $key HEAD -- . 2>$null)
'workspace key occurrences in HEAD tree files: {0}' -f $hits.Count
if ($hits.Count) { $hits | ForEach-Object { '  ' + $_ } }
$histHits = @(git log --all --format='%h' -S $key 2>$null)
'commits whose diff adds/removes the key (all refs): {0}' -f $histHits.Count
$generic = @(git grep -n -I -E -e 'sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}' -e 'xai-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}' -e 'ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}' -e 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}' -e '-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----' -e 'tskey-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}' -e 'X-Api-Key:\s*[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}' HEAD -- . 2>$null)
'generic credential pattern hits in HEAD: {0}' -f $generic.Count
$generic | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { '  ' + ($_ -replace '([A-Za-z0-9_-]{6})[A-Za-z0-9_-]{14,}', '$1<masked>') }
$raw = 'docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/response.jsonl'
$pub = 'docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/response.public.jsonl'
$rawText = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path $raw))
$pubText = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path $pub))
$rawCount = ([regex]::Matches($rawText, [regex]::Escape($key))).Count
$pubCount = ([regex]::Matches($pubText, [regex]::Escape($key))).Count
'raw key occurrences={0} public key occurrences={1}' -f $rawCount, $pubCount
'raw sha256={0} public sha256={1}' -f (Get-FileHash $raw).Hash, (Get-FileHash $pub).Hash
Get-Content 'docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/response.public-manifest.json'
$replacement = $null
$m = Get-Content 'docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/response.public-manifest.json' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
foreach ($p in $m.PSObject.Properties) { if ($p.Name -match 'replacement|placeholder|token') { $replacement = [string]$p.Value } }
if ($replacement) {
    $restored = $pubText.Replace($replacement, $key)
    'public with placeholder->key equals raw: {0}' -f ($restored -ceq $rawText)
}
'raw response tracked: ' + [bool](git ls-files -- $raw)
'raw response ignored: ' + $(git check-ignore -q -- $raw; $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)
foreach ($f in 'docs/receipts/hv/20261109T042918-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv/visible-chat-unredacted-current-session.jsonl', 'docs/receipts/hv/20261109T074610-four-agent-reasoning-claude-hv-r13/codex-chat-unredacted-current-rollout.jsonl', 'docs/receipts/hv/20261107T234831-four-agent-reasoning-grok-hv/visible-chat-unredacted-complete.md') {
    $c = 0

    '{0}: lines containing key={1} tracked={2}' -f $f, $c, [bool](git ls-files -- $f)
}
